title: NVIDIA expands supply chain commitments for AI infrastructure
html:
NVIDIA is stepping up its investments in semiconductor manufacturing and packaging capacity through expanded agreements with key supply chain partners in Taiwan, South Korea and the US. The commitments aim to secure production capacity for current and next-generation AI accelerators as demand for AI infrastructure continues to grow.

The agreements highlight the growing importance of advanced substrates, chip packaging and manufacturing capacity in scaling AI hardware. For the European semiconductor industry, they also offer insight into how NVIDIA’s long-term supply commitments are shaping global investment in chip production technologies.

NVIDIA boosts advanced substrate capacity

NVIDIA is expanding its substrate supply agreements with Kinsus Interconnect Technology and Samsung Electro-Mechanics to increase manufacturing capacity and improve production capabilities.

Under a new multiyear agreement, Kinsus will increase its advanced ABF package substrate capacity dedicated to NVIDIA by more than 3.5 times at its Youth campus in Taoyuan, Taiwan.

Production is scheduled to begin in the second half of 2027, with the additional capacity targeted for the third quarter of 2028.

Samsung Electro-Mechanics is also upgrading operational capabilities at existing factories in Sejong and Busan, South Korea, under an amended supply agreement covering NVIDIA’s computing and high-speed networking platforms.

“Our supply chain is a strategic advantage,” said Debora Shoquist, executive vice president of operations at NVIDIA. “Our work with these partners builds on our manufacturing foundation for long-term growth, expanding capacity across components, advanced packaging and system production to deliver the accelerated computing platforms our customers need.”

Nearly $3 billion for Amkor packaging expansion

Advanced packaging is another major focus, with NVIDIA backing manufacturing expansions at Amkor Technology and Siliconware Precision Industries (SPIL).

Multiyear agreements announced in July and October 2026 commit nearly $3 billion to support Amkor’s advanced packaging expansion in Arizona and South Korea. The arrangements include prepayments to help secure capacity for future AI platforms.

Meanwhile, NVIDIA is providing multibillion-dollar funding to expand SPIL’s advanced packaging operations in Taiwan.

The project includes new production lines for bumping, interposer wafer fabrication, assembly and testing, with additional contracted capacity dedicated to NVIDIA expected by mid-2029.

Vera Rubin enters volume production

NVIDIA also confirmed that its Vera Rubin NVL72 systems and Vera CPUs began volume shipments in the third quarter of 2026.

Designed for agentic AI workloads, the platforms use TSMC’s 5nm and 3nm process technologies alongside its CoWoS advanced packaging technology.

Foxconn is also expanding its collaboration with NVIDIA on next-generation GPU and networking platforms, leveraging manufacturing operations across Asia, North America and Europe.

The latest commitments build on earlier supply chain expansion plans targeting a 2.5-fold increase in substrate capacity over three years, doubled semiconductor testing capacity between 2026 and 2027, and a 15-fold increase in SPIL’s optical-engine capacity by mid-2027.
